title: Syntax: comparison, negation, linking
about: Greek needs *δεν* even when *κανείς*, *τίποτα* or *ποτέ* is already in the sentence. Comparatives are formed once, with *πιο* or with *-τερος*, never both, and "than" before a noun or pronoun is *από*. Many English linkers have their own Greek pattern: *τόσο… που/ώστε* "so… that", *ίδιος με* "the same as", *παρόλο που* "although".

items.en: Nobody came to the party.

errs.why: Greek needs *δεν* alongside *κανείς*, *τίποτα*, *ποτέ*: *κανείς δεν ήρθε*, *δεν είδα τίποτα*.

items.en: This wine is better than the other one.

errs.why: *καλύτερο* already means "better"; adding *πιο* doubles the comparative. Use one or the other: *καλύτερο* or *πιο καλό*.

items.en: Giannis is taller than me.

errs.why: "Than" before a noun or pronoun is *από* + accusative.

items.en: I didn't understand anything.

parts: Δεν μου αρέσει ούτε το τσάι ούτε ο καφές.
items.en: I like neither tea nor coffee.
items.why: Nothing to fix: *ούτε… ούτε* also needs *δεν* with the verb.

items.en: Your phone is the same as mine.

errs.why: "The same as" is *ίδιος με*: *ίδιο με το δικό μου*.

items.en: I've never been to Rhodes.
It was the biggest earthquake of the decade.

errs.why: The superlative is article + comparative: *ο μεγαλύτερος* or *ο πιο μεγάλος*. Never both.

items.en: He asked me whether I wanted coffee.

errs.why: A reported yes/no question uses *αν* alone. Greek keeps the original tense: *θέλω*.

items.en: She was so tired that she fell asleep on the sofa.

errs.why: "So… that" is *τόσο… που* (everyday) or *τόσο… ώστε* (formal). *Ότι* is a calque.

parts: Είναι η πρώτη φορά που έρχομαι στην Κέρκυρα.
items.en: It's the first time I've come to Corfu.
items.why: Nothing to fix: *η πρώτη φορά που* + present, where English uses the perfect.

items.en: Although it was raining, we went for a walk.

errs.why: "Although" is *παρόλο που*, *αν και* or *μολονότι*. *Παρόλο* does not combine with *ότι*.

items.en: The more you read, the more you learn.

errs.why: "The more… the more" is *όσο… τόσο*: *όσο περισσότερο…, τόσο περισσότερο…*.

items.en: The book I read was gripping.

errs.why: Use either *που* or *ο οποίος*, never both together.

items.en: The situation is worse than we thought.

errs.why: Before a clause, "than" is *απ' ό,τι* (or *παρά* in some set patterns, *προτιμώ να φύγω παρά να μείνω*). After a comparative with a clause, *απ' ό,τι* is the normal choice.

parts: Δεν ήρθε κανείς από τους συναδέλφους, ούτε καν ο προϊστάμενος.
items.en: None of the colleagues came, not even the boss.
items.why: Nothing to fix: *δεν… κανείς* and *ούτε καν* "not even".

items.en: The minister, whose proposal was rejected, resigned.

errs.why: "Whose" is *του οποίου* (*της οποίας*, *των οποίων*) placed before the noun: *του οποίου η πρόταση*.

items.en: I'd rather walk than take a taxi.

errs.why: Before a *να* clause "than / rather than" is *παρά*: *προτιμώ να περπατήσω παρά να πάρω ταξί*.

items.en: The matter is not as serious as you think.

errs.why: "As… as" is *τόσο… όσο*: *τόσο σοβαρό όσο νομίζεις*.

items.en: The minister never stated anything of the kind.

errs.why: Learned negative words such as *ουδέποτε* and *ουδείς* are already negative and take no *δεν*. Everyday *ποτέ* and *κανείς* do need it: *δεν δήλωσε ποτέ*.

parts: Η πόλη δεν είναι μόνο όμορφη
items.en: The city is not only beautiful but also safe.

errs.why: "Not only… but also" is *όχι μόνο… αλλά και* / *δεν… μόνο… αλλά και*.

parts: Ουδείς γνώριζε την αλήθεια, ούτε καν οι στενοί του συνεργάτες.
items.en: No one knew the truth, not even his close associates.
items.why: Nothing to fix: *ουδείς* is negative by itself and takes no *δεν*.
